outcome: Poor neonatal outcome (Apgar score <7 at 5 min, neonatal death, or meconium aspiration)
cohort: 58,964 women with one previous birth and uncomplicated singleton pregnancies at ≥ 41+3 weeks of gestation
finding: Among two-parous women with uncomplicated pregnancies at ≥ 41+3 weeks of gestation, labor induction was associated with an increased risk of cesarean section and poor neonatal outcome.
mod_finding: The study found that labor induction in prolonged pregnancies was associated with an increased risk of Cesarean section, and the success rate of vaginal delivery after induction was influenced by the mode of delivery in the first labor.
